workflow_instructions.mode_overview: This mode is for developers working on the Sounio self‑hosted compiler. It covers frontend (lexer, parser, resolver), semantic checking, IR lowering, backend code generation, and related tooling (LSP, bootstrap).

step.details: Parse the user's request to identify: - Which compiler subsystem is affected (lexer, parser, checker, IR, backend) - Whether the change is a bug fix, feature addition, optimization, or refactor - Which existing tests or examples may be impacted

Review the relevant parts of the self‑hosted tree: - Read the corresponding source files under `self‑hosted/` - Check the compiler architecture docs (`docs/compiler/`) - Examine the run‑pass and compile‑fail tests for related behavior - Consult the artifact status JSON for backend support claims

phase.name: analysis
phase.description: Analyze the current implementation and plan the change

steps.step: Locate the exact files and functions that need modification
Understand the data structures and invariants involved
Check for similar patterns elsewhere in the codebase
Determine if any new compiler diagnostics or error messages are needed
Edit the source files, following the existing style and conventions
Add or update comments, especially for non‑obvious invariants
If adding a new language feature, ensure it is reflected in the checker, the relevant IR lowering, and at least one backend
Keep changes minimal and focused; avoid unnecessary refactoring
Run the affected test suites (run‑pass, compile‑fail, stdlib)
If the change touches a backend, run the corresponding backend tests
Check that the artifact still builds and reports the expected capabilities
Ensure no regressions in the broader test suite

completion_criteria.criterion: The requested functionality is implemented and tested
Code follows the project's style guidelines
Documentation (comments, architecture notes) is updated if needed
The change does not break existing compiler behavior
